name: Arena Night A — Host Visual Acceptance
purpose: Judge whether a host implementation preserves the selected A direction as a cohesive competitive arena scene instead of a branded sticker collage.

rules: PASS requires total >= 82, zero hard blockers, and every core dimension at or above its dimension floor.
REVISE requires total 72–81, zero hard blockers, and no core dimension below 60% of its maximum.
FAIL applies to total < 72, any hard blocker, or any core dimension below its floor.
Build success, platform import, brand logo, official assets, and correct business behavior cannot compensate for a visual hard blocker.

dimensions.label: 群像关系与事件性
dimensions.question: Does the first screen depict one shared competitive event, with subjects visibly reacting to the same action?
fullScoreEvidence: At least two meaningful subjects or forces form a visible relationship: confrontation, pursuit, support, or audience reaction.
The protagonist is embedded in the arena action rather than floating as a mascot cutout.
Foreground effects, secondary character, crowd and arena all reinforce the same frozen moment.
automaticFailureSignals: A single isolated character pasted on an unrelated background.
Cards, characters and photography appear as independent stickers with no shared action.
The hero can lose every secondary layer without changing its story.

dimensions.label: 空间纵深与透视
dimensions.question: Can the viewer read foreground, action plane and arena/background as one space?
fullScoreEvidence: Clear near/mid/far depth with intentional overlap and scale progression.
Subject feet/body, effects and architecture agree on horizon and camera angle.
Cropping suggests the scene continues beyond the viewport without looking accidental.
automaticFailureSignals: Every asset sits on the same flat z-plane.
Scale or camera angle makes a character/card visibly incompatible with the background.
Large empty space isolates the hero instead of creating cinematic breathing room.

dimensions.label: 光源、色温与材质统一
dimensions.question: Do all prominent layers appear illuminated by the same arena environment?
fullScoreEvidence: One dominant key light plus a coherent secondary arena/rim light.
Highlights, shadows, bloom and atmospheric haze share direction and color temperature.
Cutout edges and contrast are integrated into the scene rather than revealing asset provenance.
automaticFailureSignals: Photographic background and cartoon/3D foreground retain incompatible lighting.
A glowing effect exists but does not illuminate nearby subjects or environment.
Different assets have visibly unrelated black levels, sharpness or shadow language.

dimensions.label: 主次层级与首屏节奏
dimensions.question: Is there one immediate focal story, followed by a legible title and a clear primary action?
fullScoreEvidence: One dominant focal subject/action is understood in under two seconds.
Secondary character/effects frame the focal point rather than competing with it.
Navigation, title and search occupy protected contrast zones and do not cover faces or critical action.
The first continuation module does not repeat the same visual story at equal strength.
automaticFailureSignals: Logo, title, cards, mascot, capsule and CTA all compete in one zone.
The hero and the next module both act as separate dominant VS moments.
Text is placed over uncontrolled detail without a stable contrast field.

dimensions.label: 品牌辨识与竞技语义
dimensions.question: After masking logos and explicit Pokémon words, does the composition still read as an energetic collectible-battle world?
fullScoreEvidence: Recognizable collectible-battle relationship, arena energy and character-led spectacle remain after blind masking.
Yellow/red/blue are used as dramatic roles, not merely decorative blocks.
At least three strong signals across asset, composition and light/effect dimensions each occupy meaningful viewport area.
automaticFailureSignals: Recognition depends mainly on logo or a single mascot.
Removing character cutouts leaves a generic esports or dark-card app.
Brand color and cards are present but do not create a brand-specific world.

dimensions.label: A 方向还原度
dimensions.question: Does the implementation preserve the selected A composition contract rather than merely its dark palette?
fullScoreEvidence: Cinematic full-height stage dominates the first viewport.
Character confrontation, audience/arena context, explosive action light and integrated search are all represented.
The emotional promise remains: competitive heat, decisive next match, and spectacle.
automaticFailureSignals: Only dark background, yellow accent and Pokémon imagery survive.
The selected group composition is replaced by a single mascot or tournament photograph.
Implementation introduces a different hero story than the approved preview.

dimensions.label: 宿主可用性与平台适配
dimensions.question: Can users still identify the page, search decks, switch plaza/event, and operate native mini-app controls safely?
fullScoreEvidence: Native capsule has a protected no-content/no-tap zone.
Custom navigation respects status bar and capsule bounds across target devices.
Page identity, search and tab state are readable and immediately operable.
Hero crop remains useful at narrow width and does not hide the primary subject or CTA.
automaticFailureSignals: Content or avatar collides with the native capsule/status area.
Search placeholder/action is illegible or visually appears disabled when usable.
Page switching or filtering becomes visually ambiguous.
The hero consumes the first screen without exposing a usable primary task.

globalHardBlockers.test: Two or more high-salience assets retain visibly independent light, scale, edge or perspective and do not form one event.
The principal character has no relational subject, environmental reaction or action consequence.
The implementation preserves colors/assets but replaces the chosen A group composition and emotional promise.
Dominant foreground and background layers cannot plausibly share a key light and environment.
Custom content intrudes into status/capsule safe zones or competes with native chrome.
The cinematic treatment makes search, tab state or page identity unclear or unusable.

reviewProtocol.blindPass: First judge screenshot with logo and explicit Pokémon words masked; then unmask for fidelity and provenance checks.
reviewProtocol.comparison: Place reference and implementation at equal viewport height; score only what is visibly rendered.
reviewProtocol.independence: QA must not receive implementation rationale or reuse a previous verdict.
